newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trygg-Hansa to buy back shares.
newsitem.headline: Trygg-Hansa to buy back shares.

text.p: Swedish insurance company Trygg-Hansa AB said on Thursday it would buy back two billion crowns ($271.1 million) worth of B-series shares at a price three percent below their market price.
Trygg-Hansa said in a statement that two major owners, Swedish insurance company SPP and Trygg-Hansa Liv, had agreed to guarantee the buy-back.
Market players had speculated the company would announce some sort of share redemption programme after trading in Tyrgg-Hansa shares was suspended before the market opened on Thursday.

"Trygg-Hansa's two largest owners, Trygg-Hansa Liv and SPP, have pledged to offer so many shares that the buy-back can be fully carried out regardless of whether other shareholders agree to take part," Trygg-Hansa said in a statement.

Trygg-Hansa said the buy-back price, three percent under the market price, meant that other shareholders probably should carefully consider participating in the buy-back and may want to remain shareholders.

If only Trygg-Hansa Liv and SPP participate in the buy-back, Trygg-Hansa Liv's stake in Trygg-Hansa will amount to 39.4 percent of the votes and a minimum of 23.3 percent of capital compared to a current holding of 39.4 percent of votes and 26.2 percent of capital.
